features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: The level of formal relevant technical education or advanced degree attainment the letter presents.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical background only.
Master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Direct experience designing agent-based systems with bounded autonomy, supervision, guardrails, or control infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: Gives no evidence of agentic-system design.
Mentions AI systems or automation without describing agent design.
Describes building agentic tooling with Python agents supported by backend services.
Explains concrete autonomy controls such as permissions, contracts, auditing, supervision, or bounded execution.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Evidence of practical data-structure and algorithmic reasoning used to improve real systems.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Hands-on production experience with AI or LLM features, especially with evaluation, reliability, and failure-mode awareness.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Developer enablement philosophy
features.description: Whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers and internal users do the secure thing by default, reflecting an enabling security philosophy rather than policing.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: How consistently the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, scope, outcomes, or impact.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims, values, or adjectives.
Includes some examples, but the work or outcome remains vague.
Gives concrete examples of what was built, changed, or owned.
Gives concrete examples plus clear mechanisms, outcomes, or measurement that make the impact easy to trust.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: How strongly the letter establishes Go as a central, production-level language in the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: Go is only briefly mentioned or not tied to meaningful ownership.
Go appears in recent work but not as a dominant language.
Go is clearly a main language for backend or service work.
Go is framed as the primary or daily-driver language with substantial system ownership.

features.name: Language breadth
features.description: The range of programming languages the letter shows beyond the core Go requirement.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.

features.name: Narrative cohesion and voice
features.description: Whether the letter presents a coherent, memorable, well-shaped story or thesis rather than a disconnected or formulaic list.

levels.descriptor: Reads as transactional or template-like, with little memorable voice.
Clear and competent but conventional.
Has a noticeable voice or coherent personal arc that helps the reader remember the candidate.
Uses distinctive framing and a well-integrated story that actively strengthens the case for fit.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Ongoing adversarial security practice outside routine development work, especially through CTFs or similar exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Responsibility for software used beyond the applicant's employer through open-source contribution, maintenance, releases, or upstream fixes.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution or maintenance is mentioned.
Mentions occasional upstream patches or contributions.
Shows maintenance responsibility for a project or library used by others.
Shows active stewardship of an externally used project, including reviews, releases, roadmap, or a real user community.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: The technical ambition, rigor, and relevance of self-directed projects outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or simple side project with limited technical stretch.
Describes a substantial side project with nontrivial systems or reliability concerns.
Describes an ambitious systems project that tackles distributed systems, storage, recovery, consensus, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: How strongly the applicant is motivated by foundational platform work whose impact compounds across many teams or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production software track record
features.description: The depth of directly relevant professional experience building, shipping, operating, testing, and maintaining production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Meets the baseline only, with limited scope or a small number of launched systems described.
Shows a solid early-career record, with several years and some repeated launch or maintenance work.
Shows a strong mid-career record, with multiple launches and clear production breadth.
Presents an extensive record for this role, combining years, repeated launches, and broad responsibility across production systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: How convincingly the letter shows substantial, production-grade Python experience for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only named briefly.
Python is mentioned as a tool the applicant uses.
Shows substantial Python use in production tooling, services, or automation.
Shows deep Python ownership across multiple relevant uses such as agents, analysis, automation, and internal services.

features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: Whether the applicant emphasizes maintainability, correctness, testing, failure awareness, and long-term operability as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific fit
features.description: How specifically the letter explains interest in this exact role and maps the applicant's background to the posting's stated responsibilities and qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Shows little role-specific motivation beyond wanting a software job or a brand-name employer.
Mentions security, scale, or Google in broad terms without a strong personal rationale.
Gives a clear role-relevant reason for interest, such as secure-by-default tooling or scaling scarce security effort.
Presents a precise, memorable thesis for wanting this role that is tightly tied to the team's mandate and the applicant's own priorities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: The extent of hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues and validating fixes or remediations.

levels.descriptor: No security assessment work is mentioned.
Mentions security reviews or assessments only in general terms.
Describes concrete assessment work such as threat models, design reviews, or attack-surface analysis.
Shows repeated, substantive assessment work with follow-through such as documented findings, remediation validation, or attacker-style code reading.

features.name: Security automation understanding
features.description: How well the letter understands the team's core problem as scaling security work through automation, triage, tooling, and AI-assisted workflows.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security collaboration orientation
features.description: Whether the applicant presents themselves as ready to partner closely and humbly with security specialists rather than operating alone.

levels.descriptor: No collaboration signal appears beyond applying for the role.
Cross-functional work is implied, but the posture toward security specialists is not explicit.
The letter explicitly shows enthusiasm for close collaboration with security engineers or learning from specialist teammates.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: The strength and relevance of formal external security certifications or credentials cited in the letter.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A foundational certification such as Security+ is cited.
A hands-on practical certification such as OSCP is cited.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability or security-report intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: The surface professionalism of the letter's writing, including proofreading, grammar, spelling, and copy accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to any broader recurring construct above.

levels.descriptor: No security engagement outside day-job claims is shown.
A modest external signal is shown, such as casual CTF participation or a baseline security credential.
A strong external signal is shown, such as serious competitive CTF results or a hands-on credential like OSCP.
Multiple strong external signals are shown, such as both high-level CTF performance and a hands-on offensive certification.
